The regional flow systems are recharged from outcrop areas on the eastern flank of the Bighorn uplift and flow down the structure into the Powder River basin. Aquifers in the regional flow system are the Lakota Sandstone Member of the Cloverly Formation of Cretaceous age (U.S. Bureau of Indian Affairs, 1974), the Madison Limestone of Mississippian age and the Red River Formation of Ordovician age (Westmoreland Resources 1975 1, p. 21).
The base of the shallow, fresh water flow system in the Project Area is the Hell Creek Formation. Ground water in Tracts II and Tract III can be considered in terms of several flow systems defined in terms of direction of flow and areas of recharge and discharge. Ground-water recharge is from precipitation, either as direct infiltration or infiltration from overland flow. In the local flow system ground-water discharge is through the more permeable beds to springs, seepage to the alluvium and through the alluvium to nearby creeks. An intermediate flow system underlies the local flow systems and from it water flows northward to discharge near the Yellowstone River.
The deep regional flow system is recharged in outcrop areas on the east flank of the Bighorn Mountains and flow is to the northeast. These aquifers have relatively high potentiometric heads, and wells located in valleys or at low elevations that penetrate these aquifers have artesian flow. The deeper aquifers have calcium sulfate water and may contain hydrogen sulfide. They are effectively separated from each other by poorly permeable strata and are separated from the shallower fresh water flow system by several thousand feet of Cretaceous shale.
